# Review: `07901b22` (feat(sentry): surface refused stub inventory) vs `base`

**Target pinned:** single commit `07901b22` against `base` = `efcfb16d`. 9 files, +628/−7 total, **+327/−7 non-test**. Working tree clean apart from the untracked `.skill/` (skill payload, not part of the change). Nothing moved under me mid-review.

**Second-model side channel:** ran (`~/.claude/bin/codex-review.sh base`, gpt-5.6-sol @ high, report at `.reviews/codex-review-20260827-200821.md`, gitignored). It confirmed finding 1 independently and returned nothing else. Findings 2–4 are mine and it did not examine them.

---

## Fix before merge

### 1. `docs/notes/sentry-triage-pipeline.md:1029` — the new attribution paragraph is contradicted by the code and by page's own text 20 lines above

> "No stage performs automatic review, retry, or label removal for this cluster."

`FIX_REFUSED_LABEL` (`"sentry:fix-refused"`) is a member of `REOPEN_SHED_LABELS` — `scripts/sentry/triage/sentry-triage-queue-contract.mjs:274`. The ingest chokepoint sheds that whole list on regression *and* on any re-verdict, so a stage does automatically remove the terminal label. Line 1004 of this same document already says exactly that: *"a `sentry:fix-pr-opened` / `sentry:fix-refused` block lifts … when the blocking stub's Sentry issue regresses and `requeueQueueStub` sheds it (`REOPEN_SHED_LABELS`), or when a human removes it."*

That sentence is load-bearing for the paragraph's conclusion ("operator-induced retries, not selector lag"). Consequence: an operator who sees the same stub refused twice reads this note, rules out the automatic path, and goes looking for a human who removed labels — when a Sentry regression on that issue produces the identical signature with nobody involved.

Confirmed by reading `sentry-triage-queue-contract.mjs:270–285`. Remedy: scope the claim to what's true — e.g. "the only automatic removal of `sentry:fix-refused` is the ingest regression/re-verdict shed (`REOPEN_SHED_LABELS`); neither run for #1304/#1313 followed a regression." One sentence, no code change.

---

## Follow-up, not blocking

### 2. `scripts/sentry/autofix/sentry-autofix-run-record.mjs:67` — the repo default is dead for the only caller shape; omitting the flag yields `github.com/null` links

`readFlag` returns `null` for an absent flag (`sentry-autofix-finalize.mjs:710-715`). `sentry-autofix-finalize.mjs:853` passes that straight through as `refusedInventoryRepo`. A JS default parameter fires only on `undefined`, so `repo` becomes `null`.

Reproduced against this commit:

```
$ node .../sentry-autofix-finalize.mjs run-record ... \
    --refused-inventory '{"state":"known","count":2,"issues":[1304,1313]}'
- Refused stubs (all states): 2 ([#1304](https://github.com/null/issues/1304), [#1313](https://github.com/null/issues/1313))
```

The production workflow always passes `--refused-inventory-repo "${REPO}"` (`sentry-autofix.yml:1451`) so the tracker comment is unaffected today. But the CLI usage block the change added (`sentry-autofix-finalize.mjs:690`) presents the two flags as independently optional, so this is a documented-and-broken path. `--refused-inventory-repo ""` gives the same class (`https://github.com//issues/…`).

Remedy: `readFlag(args, "--refused-inventory-repo") ?? undefined`, or normalize nullish/empty inside `renderRefusedStubInventory`. The new tests only exercise the `unknown` branch through the CLI, which never reads `repo` — that's why it slipped.

### 3. `scripts/sentry/autofix/sentry-autofix-refused-inventory.mjs:26` — a wrong-but-well-formed query renders a confident `0`, not `unknown`

The module header sells this as fail-closed, and the parsing genuinely is. But a query that simply matches nothing returns `{"total_count":0,"incomplete_results":false,"items":[]}`, which passes every validator and renders `- Refused stubs (all states): 0`. A label rename, a typo, or Search index lag right after a labelling run therefore reports a clean zero rather than degrading. Given the new doc paragraph tells operators five stubs (#1304, #1313, #1316, #1326, #1328) are outstanding, a silent `0` is the one wrong answer that reads as good news.

Confirmed by reading `parseRefusedStubInventory:63-95` — there is no path from "empty result" to `unknown` by design.

Cheapest remedy: keep the zero, but make it verifiable — assert the query matched the tracker's own known-refused floor, or render `0` distinctly (e.g. `0 (no refused stubs matched)`), so an operator can tell "none" from "query found none."

### 4. `scripts/sentry/autofix/sentry-autofix-refused-inventory.mjs:26` — the only unquoted colon-label search query in the repo, and the only one built from literals

Two divergences from the surrounding code, both one-line fixes:

- **Quoting.** Every other search call site quotes label values: `sentry-autofix-queue-io.mjs:278` (`-label:"${FIX_REFUSED_LABEL}"` ×5), `sentry-autofix-family-handled.mjs:144`, `sentry-autofix-reverse-verify.mjs:222`. This one emits bare `label:sentry:fix-refused`, a value containing a colon. **Unconfirmed** — `gh` is disabled in this checkout so I could not run the query, and I found no comment in the repo explaining the quoting convention. If GitHub's parser mishandles it, the failure mode is finding 3: a silent `0`. Quoting costs nothing and matches every sibling.
- **Literals vs constants.** The query hardcodes `sentry-triage` and `sentry:fix-refused` instead of importing `SENTRY_TRIAGE_QUEUE_LABEL` (`sentry-autofix-queue-io.mjs:39`) and `FIX_REFUSED_LABEL` (`sentry-triage-queue-contract.mjs:191`), which every other call site imports. A future label rename updates the constants and the selector, and leaves this inventory reporting `0` forever. Same for `DEFAULT_REPO` at line 15.

---

## Considered and cleared

- **Suite-gate manifest / snapshot isolation.** The new `readFileSync` line-cap test reads two `.mjs` files by URL; the manifest doc warns an undeclared `reads:` entry fails the suite. Both files are in the test's import closure, so they land in the snapshot — verified by running `scripts/sentry/gate/sentry-suite-gate.mjs`: all 14 suites green, run-record `pass=23 floor=7`. Floors left at their old values is explicitly sanctioned by the manifest `_readme` ("adding tests never breaks the gate"), not drift worth chasing.
- **Quality-gate routing.** `agent-quality-gate.test.sh:4415` asserts the new file routes to both focused suites; the gate script change at `agent-quality-gate.sh:4091` matches. Consistent.
- **Workflow wiring.** `GH_TOKEN` and `REPO` are in the step's `env` (`sentry-autofix.yml:1322-1323`); the step is `continue-on-error: true` under `set -uo pipefail` (no `-e`); `|| printf '{"state":"unknown"}'` plus `main()`'s internal catch means the helper cannot red the run or block the upsert. The 15 s child deadline sits well inside the job's `timeout-minutes: 5`.
- **`runGhWithTimeout` settle logic.** Checked the kill-path races: settle-before-kill, `clearKillTimer` on both `close` and `error`, `terminated === false` → immediate SIGKILL, spawn-throw before listeners attach. No double-settle and no leaked timer found.
- **Body-builder blast radius.** `buildAutofixRunRecordBody` has exactly one non-test caller; nothing in the repo parses the run-record lines, so the inserted line breaks no consumer. Both focused suites pass (finalize 65, run-record 23).
- **Mechanical.** `git diff --check` clean; no tabs in the new file; no conflict markers; no credentials or secret-shaped content in the change.
- **Not raised as findings:** Search API eventual consistency (the inventory is report-only and feeds no decision — the codex pass flagged it, I agree it's acceptable); the `+N more` / `total_count` arithmetic, which is correct including the count-0 and count>10 cases.

## What I could not do

- **`gh` is disabled in this checkout** ("gh is disabled during evaluation"), so no live Search API call. Finding 4's quoting half is unverified against GitHub, and the query's real-world result shape is unverified.
- **`scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh` did not complete** — killed at the 10-minute ceiling (exit 143). The codex pass reported it failing in a process-drain fixture unrelated to this change; either way, that suite is **uncovered here**, including the two assertions this change adds to it. Someone should run it to completion.
- `~/.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview` does not exist on this machine; the repo-local `pnpm agent:autoreview` adapter was not run. The second-model coverage I got is the `codex-review.sh` pass only.
- Everything above is established by **reading source and running two focused Node suites plus the sentry suite gate**. Nothing here proves the workflow runs: the new helper has never executed against the live Search API, and the rendered tracker comment has never been produced end-to-end. Outstanding proof: one real `record-run` execution on `main` with the tracker comment inspected.

## Verdict

**Does not pass as-is** — finding 1 is a documentation claim the repository contradicts, in an operator runbook, and it is a one-sentence fix. Findings 2–4 are non-blocking. The runtime behaviour of the production workflow path is sound as far as reading can establish. This is not a substitute for the repo's own merge gate, which includes the quality-gate self-test I could not finish.
other_review:
The main workflow path is functional, but a documented valid CLI form emits malformed links. The change also omits the repository-required registry entry for its new workflow path pin.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Preserve the default repository when the flag is omitted — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1984-07901b22c0da/scripts/sentry/autofix/sentry-autofix-finalize.mjs:853-853
  When `run-record` receives a known `--refused-inventory` without the optional `--refused-inventory-repo`, `readFlag` returns `null`. Passing that value explicitly bypasses the renderer's default parameter and produces links such as `https://github.com/null/issues/123`. Use the default repository when this flag is absent, or require both flags together.

- [P2] Register the new workflow path pin — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1984-07901b22c0da/.github/workflows/sentry-autofix.yml:1418-1419
  This exact workflow callsite creates a new `scripts/` path pin, but `scripts/AGENTS.md:118-119` requires every new pin to be listed. If this module later moves, the stale call will quietly fall back to `unknown` on every run instead of failing, so the inventory can remain broken unnoticed. Add this workflow execution pin to the documented pin inventory.
